comment: Injected into the stock LaTeX grammar wherever it has already established a tikzpicture. The negations matter: inside a tikzpicture, maths, comments and verbatim are ordinary LaTeX and must be left alone, and excluding them here is what keeps every rule below free of guards.

picture-body.comment: Path level: what a tikzpicture body looks like outside an option list. Shared with the toplevel grammar so an inline \tikz...; one-liner is tokenised identically.

maths.comment:
Maths is a different language embedded in the figure, and is scoped as one flat string so it reads as content rather than as more TikZ. The host grammar was doing this until now, and its scopes are the problem: a control sequence in maths is constant.other.general.math.tex, which nearly every theme colours from the same family as variable -- the family a \def'ed macro already gets from the semantic provider. Two ambers, and no way to tell a macro from an \varepsilon. A string scope is both distinct in every theme measured and what the host grammar half-says already, since it calls the delimiters punctuation.definition.string.

The cost is the internal structure of a formula: subscripts, digits and \alpha are now one colour. In a figure a formula is a label a few characters long, and knowing where it begins and ends is worth more than colouring inside it.

Every rule bails out at \end{...}, so an unclosed $ costs one label rather than the rest of the file.

comment.comment: Opening a block below takes tokenisation of its interior away from the host, so comments inside an option list are ours to handle.
comment.name: comment.line.percentage.tikz

option-list.comment: A bracketed option list. Bailing out at \end{...} keeps an unbalanced bracket from swallowing the rest of the picture.

value-group.comment: A braced value: a nested key list (every node/.style={...}), or node text, or maths. Recursing into the option body handles the first and is harmless for the rest.

style-handle.comment: name/.style = {...} and friends. Matched before #key so the handle does not read as an ordinary key.

key.comment: Any word phrase followed by '='. Deliberately generic: this covers every built-in key (dash pattern, line width, minimum size, inner sep) and every custom one, with no vocabulary to maintain. The trailing [<>] catches 'shorten >='. A comma cannot appear in the class, so a key can never span two option items.

arrow.comment: Arrow tip specifications. Only reachable inside an option list, which is what separates '-|' the tip from '-|' the path join.

path-join.comment: Path joins live outside option lists, between coordinates.
path-join.name: keyword.operator.path.tikz

patterns.comment: 'at' and 'and' are ordinary English, and node text is not excluded from this injection, so they are only claimed when a coordinate follows -- which is the only way TikZ ever uses them.
patterns.name: keyword.control.path.tikz

coordinate.comment: Parentheses are marked as punctuation without claiming their interior, so node text and maths inside them keep their host tokenisation. A named coordinate is picked out separately.

_why-no-path-level-braces.comment: There is deliberately no rule marking { } at path level. An injection selected with L: outruns the host's own end patterns, so a bare '}' rule steals the closing brace of constructs like \textbf{...} and leaves them open for the rest of the file. Braces are only marked inside an option list, where #value-group opens and closes them as a matched pair and the region is genuinely ours. At path level a brace introduces node text, which is LaTeX and rightly keeps its LaTeX colours.

dimension.comment: Matched before #number so the unit is never orphaned. TeX's full unit set, plus the pgf-specific ones.
dimension.name: constant.numeric.dimension.tikz

macro.comment: A control sequence used as a value. The semantic token provider recolours the ones it can prove are \def'ed in this file; this is the fallback for the rest.
macro.name: support.function.general.tex

bare-option.comment: A valueless option or a style reference: 'thick', 'dashed', 'school axis', 'coloraqua'. Last resort, so anything with more structure has already been claimed. Every word must begin with a letter: TextMate takes the earliest match, not the first listed rule, so allowing a digit-led continuation let this swallow the numbers in 'dash pattern=on 1.6pt off 1.3pt' before #dimension could reach them.
bare-option.name: support.function.tikz entity.name.function.tikz
